title: EastWest Dream Run 2026 Iloilo Review: What the Iloilo Leg Was Like
seo_title: EastWest Dream Run 2026 Iloilo Review | Atria Park District
meta_description: EastWest Dream Run 2026 Iloilo review: more than 2,000 runners from Atria Park District on 20 September, past Jaro Cathedral and the riverfront.
dek: EastWest Bank's race series brought its Iloilo leg to Atria Park District on 20 September 2026. Here is what the race was like, from the published account of it.
verdict: The Iloilo leg of the EastWest Dream Run is a bank-sponsored family race with a proper half marathon attached. More than 2,000 people took part at Atria Park District on 20 September 2026, aged from 7 to 72, across the 21 km, 10 km, 5 km, 3 km and a 1 km dog run [1]. The route passed the Jaro Cathedral belfry and the Iloilo riverfront [1], and the 21 km was won by two elite distance runners, Rogen Aguirre and Jennylyn Nobleza [1]. If you want a well-organised city race in Iloilo that works for the whole family, it is a good one. The account available comes from the organisers' own release, so read it as that.

sections.heading: The 2026 Iloilo Leg
paragraphs: More than 2,000 runners, families and friends gathered at Atria Park District in Iloilo City for the race on Sunday 20 September 2026 [1]. It was organised by RunRio for EastWest Bank, in support of the Department of Tourism's Love the Philippines campaign [1].

The categories ran from a 1 km dog run through 3 km, 5 km and 10 km to the 21 km half marathon, and runners ranged in age from seven to 72 [1]. A nine-year-old finished second in the women's 3 km [1].

sections.heading: The Course and the Front of the Race
paragraphs: The route went through the centre of Iloilo City, past the Jaro Cathedral belfry and along the riverfront [1].

The half marathon had real quality at the front. Rogen Aguirre won the men's 21 km and Jennylyn Nobleza the women's [1]. Both were also in the Team 7-Eleven Philippines group of qualifiers sent to the Borneo International Marathon in May 2026 [2], so this was not a field of casual runners at the sharp end.

sections.heading: Should You Enter Next Year?
paragraphs: If you are in Western Visayas and want a race you can bring the family, or the dog, to, yes. There are five distances to choose from, and the release describes partner booths, games and giveaways beyond the race itself [1].

The limit of the evidence is its source: the account of the day comes from the organisers' release, which was republished by local sites. It tells you who came and who won, not how the water stations, marshalling or timing held up.
This review is compiled from the published account of the 2026 Iloilo leg. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.
